title: Evolving charge order in the CDW state of AV$_3$Sb$_5$ metals
authors: Anshu Kataria, Francis Pratt, Peter J. Baker, Stephen Cottrell, Miki Bonacci, Andrea Capa Salinas, Stephen D. Wilson, Zurab Guguchia, Samuele Sanna, Pietro Bonfà
abstract: AV$_3$Sb$_5$ kagome metals are characterized by intertwined electronic and structural orders, which motivated extensive studies in recent years. Yet the details of the electronic state preceding the superconducting phase remain poorly understood. Here we extend our previous investigation [Phys. Rev. Research 7, L032046 (2025)] of RbV$_3$Sb$_5$ using avoided level crossing (ALC) muon-spin spectroscopy to the $A$ = Cs and K systems. Consistent with our previous study, we identify a second transition whose origin cannot be attributed solely to an internal magnetic field, indicating the involvement of an additional electronic mechanism that subtly modifies the charge distribution within the V plane. In particular, the ALC results point towards an additional charge modulation taking place within the charge density wave (CDW) phase and occurring at $T^{*}<T_{CDW}$ for $A$ = Cs and Rb, or in the vicinity of $T_{CDW}$ for $A$ = K.
summary: This work uses muon-spin spectroscopy ($\mu	ext{SR}$) on $	ext{AV}_3	ext{Sb}_5$ kagome metals to investigate the electronic state preceding superconductivity. The key finding is the evidence for an additional charge modulation within the $	ext{CDW}$ phase, detected via $	ext{ALC}$ muon-spin spectroscopy. This suggests that the electronic order is more complex than previously modeled by magnetic field effects alone.
main_problem: The study aims to elucidate the poorly understood electronic state in $	ext{AV}_3	ext{Sb}_5$ kagome metals that exists immediately preceding the superconducting phase.
main_result: The $	ext{ALC}$-$\mu	ext{SR}$ results point towards an additional charge modulation occurring within the Charge Density Wave ($	ext{CDW}$) phase at temperatures $T^* < T_{	ext{CDW}}$ for $	ext{A} = 	ext{Cs}$ and $	ext{Rb}$.
method: The research employs Avoided Level Crossing ($	ext{ALC}$) muon-spin spectroscopy ($\mu	ext{SR}$) and Zero Field ($	ext{ZF}$)-$\mu	ext{SR}$ measurements to probe local electronic environments.
model_or_system: The physical system is the $	ext{AV}_3	ext{Sb}_5$ family of kagome metals ($	ext{A} = 	ext{K}, 	ext{Rb}, 	ext{Cs}$), which exhibit intertwined electronic and structural orders, including a $	ext{CDW}$ state.
key_observables: Muon spin relaxation rate ($\lambda$ and $\Delta$), $	ext{ALC}$ resonance dips (time-integrated asymmetry), and the temperature dependence of these observables.
important_parameters: The transition temperatures $T^*$ and $T_{	ext{CDW}}$, and the applied low longitudinal magnetic field ($	ext{LF}$).
main_assumptions: The interpretation requires considering an additional electronic mechanism beyond simple internal magnetic field contributions to explain the observed $	ext{ALC}$ transition.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temperature dependence of $	ext{ZF}$ muon asymmetry and $	ext{ALC}$-$\mu	ext{SR}$ resonance dips for $	ext{CsV}_3	ext{Sb}_5$ and $	ext{KV}_3	ext{Sb}_5$, showing field shifts and resonance area changes.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes $	ext{ALC}$-$\mu	ext{SR}$ and $	ext{ZF}$-$\mu	ext{SR}$ data across different alkali metals ($	ext{A}$), focusing on the temperature evolution of spectral features near the $	ext{CDW}$ transition to pinpoint the origin of an additional electronic modulation.
why_interesting: The use of highly sensitive local probes like $\mu	ext{SR}$ to detect subtle, temperature-dependent charge modulations within a complex correlated electronic state is relevant to understanding emergent quantum phases.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. ZF muon asymmetry, normalized to one, for (a) CsV3Sb5 and (b) KV3Sb5 at different temperatures. Data in panel (a) are from [54]. The solid lines are best fit to the Eq. 1. The insets show the relaxation rates, ∆and λ, as a function of the temperature. The dashed vertical lines in the insets represent the CDW transitions and the shaded re- gion for CsV3Sb5 represents the temperature range over which the relaxation varies and anomalies are observed in ALC measurements.

FIG. 2. Normalized TI asymmetry variation with applied field at different temperatures up to above the TCDW for (a) CsV3Sb5 and (b) KV3Sb5. Temperature-dependent resonance spectra are vertically shifted by the amounts reported in the picture for clarity. The solid colored lines represent the best fit using Eq. 2. The dashed arrow lines are guides to the eye to showcase the variation of resonance fields with increasing temperature.

FIG. 3. The top panel shows the temperature dependence of the fitting parameter for the CsV3Sb5 system, (a) area (b) width and (c) resonant field of three resonances. The bottom panel presents the same fitting parameters for KV3Sb5 system. The dashed lines, color coded according to the respective parameters, serve as guide-to-the-eye for visualizing their temperature-dependent evolution. The vertical black dot-dashed line indicates the CDW transition temperature, TCDW. Finally, the shaded region in panels (a-c) corresponds to the temperature range where anomalies are observed in both ZF and ALC µSR measurement.

FIG. 4. Experimental and simulated ALC-µSR spectra, considering the cluster of the nearest Sb atom and other six nearest V atoms (see SM) roughly forming a hexagon around the muon stopping site for (a) CsV3Sb5, (b) KV3Sb5 and (c) RbV3Sb5 (data from [53]). The y-axis represents the (normalized) time-integrated asymmetry.

FIG. 5. Perturbation induced by local fields at the muon and V sites on ZF and ALC measurements. The black line shows the results obtained with the minimal model described in the text. The shaded area highlight the changes induced by the presence of local (hyper- fine) fields of electronic origin at the muon and the V nuclei. The dotted red line in panel (b) shows the one simulation with the lowest dip resulting from the presence of local fields.
